name: Field notes / pixel signal
authorship: Original LitClaude profile outside the immutable library
hierarchy: large editorial title with intentional breaks
a tight editorial rhythm with thin rules, notebook-dot paper and a second accent
layered surfaces: a colour band, a two-accent wash and one atmosphere glow
original task-specific pixel-art illustration as the primary visual anchor when the brief gives no visual direction

density.calm_only_when: the request asks for a minimal, calm, quiet or restrained page (미니멀, 차분, 절제), or design-lock.mjs init --density calm; calm restores 64 to 128 px sections, a flat canvas and no glow

pixel_art.description: When the brief gives no visual direction, use an original, task-specific pixel-art illustration as the primary visual anchor without asking. A brief that names competing directions without choosing them is unresolved, not unspecified.
pixel_art.method: author a recognizable integer-grid motif with hard edges and nearest-neighbor scaling
pixel_art.rendering: crisp and non-smoothed; use nearest-neighbor scaling and disable interpolation
pixel_art.constraint: recognizable task-related subject, not random noise or a smooth icon

work_surfaces.applies_to: screens people work in repeatedly, such as admin consoles, analytics views and internal tools, as opposed to pages people read once
work_surfaces.first_viewport: the working content and primary controls; no hero headline, tagline or illustration block above them
work_surfaces.pixel_art: a small accent at most, never the primary visual anchor
work_surfaces.keeps: nothing of this palette: work surfaces lock the graphite house style (scripts/design-lock.mjs family default); the pixel art stays a small accent at most

responsive.rule: reflow content and line breaks, never crop the title

motion: layered motion is welcome where it explains or delights (see references/motion-guide.md); state changes remain understandable with nonessential motion disabled
precedence: explicit user direction and existing brand tokens override this default; if the brief names competing visual directions without choosing or delegating one, ask before applying it
